doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

chapter: Condon's circle and New York scene
title: Listening to pianists at Condon's as a teenager
summary: His father took him to Condon's balcony to hear Joe Sullivan, Gene Schroeder and James P. Johnson.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Right. Well your father certainly set you on a definite path then.

Oh he was great. He used to — we used to go to Eddie Condon’s, he used to take me to Eddie Condon’s when I was still young, in my teenage years. Take me to Condon’s and we’d sit up in the balcony. I was looking at the Ken Burns film the other day and it showed a shot of Condon’s and you could see the balcony. It was taken from the balcony from here, but we used to sit over here and I’d look down on the piano, the piano keyboard would be laid out there. And I’d watch Joe Sullivan and Gene Schroeder and all

the piano players that played, James P. Johnson and all those guys who used to play with Eddie. And I got a great education just listening to these guys play and how they played and how they approached the music. Subtly or unsubtly.
They probably didn’t have much music sitting in front of them, did they?

Oh no, none at all. No. I couldn’t understand that at first either. But then I got to realize you learn the songs. After I learned my first song I said ahhh, that’s how they do it. Learn the song and then go from there.
